author: Alisson Bento
title: Claimed by the Mountain Kings
text:
Copper and Skin


The freezing rain began to fall in the agonizing, pitch-black hours just before dawn, a torrential, icy Appalachian downpour that hammered against the reinforced exterior walls of the Copper Compound like a legion of desperate fists. The storm was a deafening, acoustic assault, but it wasn't loud enough to drown out the horrifying reality of what had just happened.


I paced the length of the second-floor hallway, my bare feet sinking deeply into the plush pile of the runner rug, my muscles coiled so tightly they ached. The soft gray sweatpants and oversized white cotton t-shirt Atwater had sourced from deep within a storage closet offered physical warmth, but they did absolutely nothing to thaw the solid block of glacial terror sitting squarely behind my sternum.


Just minutes ago, the absolute silence of the house had been shattered by the encrypted, localized chirp of Darell’s tactical radio. I had heard Bruno’s deep, strained voice transmitting from the freezing ridges above us. I had heard the confirmation. Priority Red. The words were a brand, searing themselves into my conscious mind. Highly trained corporate sicarios. A minimum of a five-man fireteam. Three miles from the perimeter.


Miriam’s men were in the woods. They were walking through the dark, hunting the digital ghost of my cell phone ping, closing the net around the only place on earth where I had found a sliver of safety.


A violent tremor wracked my frame, starting at my knees and vibrating up through my spine until my teeth literally chattered. It wasn't the ambient temperature of the house. The massive stone fireplace downstairs was still radiating heat, pushed through the vents by the humming HVAC system. This was the chemical fallout of pure, sustained adrenaline. My nervous system was trapped in a continuous, agonizing loop of fight-or-flight, and with the heavy steel blast doors locked down tight, flight was no longer an option.


I reached the end of the hallway, my shoulder brushing against the dark mahogany paneling. The urge to crawl into the darkest, smallest corner of the basement and curl into a fetal position was overwhelming. It was the trauma reflex, the deeply ingrained instinct Miriam had beaten into me over two years of calculated captivity. Make yourself small. Make yourself invisible. If she can't see you, she can't hurt you.


But the rules of the hollow were different. Darell had explicitly forbidden me from falling apart. He had claimed my fear as his own property, and I realized with a sudden, suffocating clarity that I could not survive the next twenty-four hours trapped alone inside my own head. If I retreated into the dark, the panic would consume me long before the cartel breached the front door.


I needed an anchor. I needed the violent, overwhelming gravity of the men who had promised to burn the world down for me.


I turned away from the shadowed stairwell and looked down the corridor. Four heavy, solid oak doors lined the hall. Three were shut tight, completely dark. But beneath the frame of the second door on the left, a thin, sharp sliver of dim yellow light cut across the floorboards.


Blake’s room.


I didn't stop to analyze the decision. If I paused to calculate the risk, the vulnerability of walking willingly into a predator's den in the middle of the night, my nerve would shatter. I moved toward the sliver of light, my strides quick and silent.


I reached the door. The thick oak muffled the sounds within, but I could hear the low, resonant hum of two distinct male voices murmuring in rapid, clipped sentences. They weren't sleeping. They were plotting.


I raised my trembling right hand and pressed my palm flat against the wood. I didn't knock. I pushed the door open.


The hinges were perfectly oiled, yielding without a sound. I stepped over the threshold into the room.


The air in Blake’s bedroom was dense, heavy with the sharp, medicinal bite of high-proof Kentucky whiskey, the metallic tang of gun oil, and the deep, clean scent of male sweat. The single bedside lamp was turned on low, casting a long, distorted pool of amber light across a massive, unmade king-sized bed. The sheets were a dark, charcoal gray, tangled in chaotic knots.


Blake was sitting on the edge of the mattress, leaning forward with his elbows resting on his spread knees. He was wearing faded, incredibly soft-looking flannel pajama pants and nothing else. His torso was a lean, heavily muscled landscape of pale skin and chaotic, stick-and-poke style tattoos that looked black in the dim light.


Directly across from him, sitting deep in the recesses of a worn leather armchair, was Atwater. The logistics manager was fully dressed in his dark denim and gray henley, his wire-rimmed glasses pushed up the bridge of his nose. A tactical map of the southern valley was spread out on the small wooden table between them, anchored at the corners by two half-empty lowball glasses and a heavy bottle of bourbon.


The moment the latch clicked, both men stopped speaking.


Their heads snapped toward the door with terrifying, synchronized speed. For a fraction of a second, I saw the raw, unfiltered lethality of the syndicate. Atwater’s hand had instantly dropped to his hip, his fingers brushing the grip of a concealed weapon. Blake’s mismatched eyes flared with a predatory, calculating light, every muscle in his chest locking tight.


Then, they registered my face.


The violent tension immediately drained from the room, replaced by a heavy, charged silence.


I stood frozen just inside the doorway, my arms wrapped tightly around my waist, my fingernails digging into my own sides. I was shaking so badly the oversized cotton t-shirt was vibrating against my skin. I couldn't form a coherent sentence. The words were trapped behind the suffocating block of panic in my throat.


Blake slowly sat back, letting his hands drop loosely onto the mattress. His gaze swept over my trembling frame, taking in my bare feet, the white-knuckle grip I had on my own ribs, and the wide, blown-out terror in my hazel eyes.


"Close the door, wildcat," Blake instructed. His voice was a low, rough purr, completely stripped of its usual teasing lilt.


I reached blindly behind me, my fingers finding the heavy brass handle. I pulled the door shut, the latch engaging with a soft click that severed us entirely from the rest of the dark house.


"You're vibrating," Atwater observed quietly from the depths of the leather armchair. He didn't reach for his bourbon. He watched me with the intense, analytical focus of a man diagnosing a complex mechanical failure. "The ambient temperature in this room is seventy-two degrees. You are experiencing acute autonomic hyperarousal."


"They're coming," I rasped, the words finally tearing loose from my throat. My voice sounded pathetic, a fragile, broken whisper against the drumming of the rain on the windowpane. "They're in the woods. Miriam sent them."


"They are three miles out," Atwater corrected, his tone incredibly calm, offering factual data to combat the irrational spiral of my panic. "The terrain is treacherous, and visibility is zero. They are moving blind. They will not reach the outer perimeter charges before dawn."


"You don't understand," I choked out, taking a halting step forward, the distance to the bed suddenly feeling like an impossibly vast ocean. "If they find the access road... if they breach the gates... she won't just kill you. She's going to make me watch."


"Nobody is breaching the gates, Callie," Blake said. He didn't raise his voice. He didn't move toward me. He simply patted the dark gray sheets right between his spread thighs. "Come here."


The invitation wasn't a request. It was a lifeline thrown into a drowning sea.


I crossed the room. My legs felt like lead, heavy and entirely uncoordinated, but the gravitational pull radiating from the bed was absolute. I reached the edge of the mattress and stopped, standing directly between Blake's knees.


He looked up at me, the emerald green and muddy brown of his eyes burning with an intense, focused heat. He could smell the fear on me. He could feel the chaotic, destructive energy threatening to tear my nervous system apart.


He reached out, his large, rough hands wrapping around my waist. The heat of his palms bled instantly through the thin cotton of my shirt, shocking my skin.


"You're trapped in your own head," Blake murmured, his thumbs pressing firmly into the soft flesh just above my hip bones. "You're living in tomorrow. Tomorrow doesn't exist yet. There is only right now. This room. This rain. Me and Atwater."


He applied a steady, downward pressure to my hips.


I didn't resist. I let my knees buckle, completely surrendering my physical autonomy to his grip. I dropped onto the mattress, straddling his lap, my shins resting on the sheets on either side of his thighs.


The physical contact was a massive, grounding shockwave. Blake’s bare chest was a furnace against the thin cotton of my shirt. I gasped, my hands flying up to grip his broad shoulders, my fingers digging desperately into the hard, tattooed muscle. I buried my face in the crook of his neck, inhaling the intoxicating, hyper-masculine scent of whiskey and sweat.


He wrapped his arms entirely around my back, crushing me flush against him. He was a solid wall of bone and muscle, an impenetrable barrier between my fragile existence and the apocalyptic threat circling outside the compound.


"That's it," Blake whispered, his breath hot against my ear. His large hand moved up my spine, his fingers tangling into the heavy mass of my dirty-blonde hair. He gripped the roots, his hold firm, possessive, anchoring my skull against his collarbone. "Give it to me. Give me the panic. You don't need to carry it anymore."


A ragged, tearing sob ripped its way out of my chest, muffled against his skin. The dam finally broke. The adrenaline crash hit me with devastating force, turning my bones to liquid. I clung to him, weeping silently, my tears hot and fast against the sensitive skin of his neck.


Blake didn't try to shush me. He didn't offer empty platitudes. He simply absorbed the breakdown, his hold unyielding, his thumb stroking a slow, heavy rhythm against the base of my skull.


Behind me, I heard the soft, deliberate scrape of the leather armchair moving.


I didn't lift my head. I didn't care. The presence of the second man didn't trigger my flight response. In the bizarre, twisted geometry of the Copper Compound, the addition of a second predator only fortified the walls of the cage.


I felt the mattress dip slightly behind me.


Atwater knelt on the bed directly behind my back. The shift in the air currents warned me a fraction of a second before his hands made contact.


Atwater’s touch was entirely different from Blake’s. Where Blake was chaotic, hot, and overwhelmingly forceful, Atwater was clinical, precise, and agonizingly deliberate.


His broad, cool hands settled over my shoulders, his long fingers pressing into the tight, knotted muscles along my trapezius.


"Your respiratory rate is elevating again," Atwater noted, his voice a low, smooth vibration that slid directly down my spine. His thumbs began to knead the tension at the base of my neck, applying a deep, localized pressure that made me whimper softly. "You are hyperventilating. Focus on the sensory input. Focus on the pressure."


I tried to pull in a deep breath, but my chest felt banded in iron.


"Look at me, Callie," Blake commanded, his hand shifting from my hair to grip my chin. He tilted my head up, forcing me to break contact with his neck and meet his gaze.


His mismatched eyes were dark, dilated, the pupils swallowing the irises. The protective instinct was rapidly mutating, bleeding into a heavy, predatory hunger. He recognized exactly what I was doing. I wasn't just seeking a hug to stop a panic attack. I was seeking oblivion. I wanted to be consumed so entirely by the physical reality of the present moment that the past and the future ceased to exist.


"You want to forget," Blake stated, his thumb brushing over my swollen, trembling lower lip. It wasn't a question.


"Make it go away," I breathed, my hands sliding from his shoulders to frame his jaw, my thumbs tracing the rough stubble on his cheeks. "Please, Blake. Turn it off."


A dark, dangerous smile curved his mouth. "Atwater," Blake said, not breaking eye contact with me. "She wants us to turn the noise off."


"Then we will recalibrate her focus," Atwater replied from behind me.


Atwater’s hands slid down from my shoulders, his palms skating over the thin cotton covering my back. He gripped the hem of my t-shirt.


He didn't ask for permission. In this room, my surrender had already been tendered the moment I closed the door behind me.


Atwater pulled the fabric upward. I raised my arms automatically, facilitating the removal. The cool air of the bedroom rushed over my heated skin for a fleeting second before the shirt was pulled over my head and discarded into the shadows beyond the bed.


I shivered, my breath catching in my throat. I was bare to the waist, exposed in the dim amber light. The jagged, ugly line of the burn scar on my collarbone felt blindingly conspicuous. For years, I had hidden my body, viewing it merely as a canvas for Miriam's cruelty.


But as Blake looked down at me, there was absolutely no pity in his eyes. There was only raw, consuming desire.


"You're perfect," Blake growled, his hands dropping to my waist. He slid his thumbs under the thick elastic waistband of the sweatpants. "Lift."


I planted my hands on his broad shoulders and pushed myself up onto my knees. Blake pulled the sweatpants down, his hands skimming over the curve of my hips and down my thighs, dragging the fabric with them until they joined the discarded shirt on the floor. I wore nothing but a pair of plain cotton underwear.


I sank back down onto his lap, my bare thighs sliding against his flannel-clad legs. The friction was electric, a sudden, searing jolt that entirely banished the lingering chill from the hallway.


Atwater moved closer behind me. His chest brushed against my bare back, the soft material of his henley providing a stunning contrast to Blake's bare, heated skin in front of me. Atwater wrapped his long arms around my waist, pulling me flush against him, sandwiching me entirely between their bodies.


I was trapped. I was completely immobilized by two hundred-and-fifty-pound men who killed for a living.


And I had never felt safer in my entire life.


"Breathe for me, Callie," Atwater murmured, his lips pressing a soft, deliberate kiss against the curve of my shoulder blade.


I inhaled sharply, the scent of the men entirely overpowering the smell of the rain.


Blake didn't wait any longer. His hands moved up my ribcage, his rough, calloused palms incredibly hot against my skin. He cupped my bare breasts, his thumbs brushing over the hardened peaks with a firm, demanding pressure.


A sharp gasp tore from my lips, my spine arching backward, pressing my shoulder blades deeper into Atwater’s solid chest.


"There it is," Blake rumbled, his eyes tracking the flush of heat spreading across my chest. "That's the frequency. Stay right there."


He leaned forward, capturing my mouth in a devastating, bruising kiss.


It was an absolute sensory assault. Blake’s mouth was hungry, chaotic, his tongue sweeping past my lips to claim the interior with a violent, intoxicating rhythm. He tasted of the expensive bourbon, a dark, burning flavor that mirrored the liquid heat pooling low in my stomach. I opened to him completely, my hands tangling in his shaggy hair, giving back the aggression measure for measure.


Behind me, Atwater’s hands were methodical. While Blake was a thunderstorm, Atwater was a surgeon. He mapped the curves of my waist and hips, his long fingers pressing deeply into the muscle tissue, grounding me in the physical reality of his touch. One of his hands slid upward, tracing the line of my sternum, before his palm flattened flat against my racing heart, feeling the frantic, galloping beat trapped beneath my ribs.


His other hand moved downward.


Atwater slipped his fingers beneath the thin cotton waistband of my underwear.


I broke the kiss with Blake, a breathless, stuttering moan escaping my lips as Atwater’s cool, precise fingers made contact with the slick, aching heat between my thighs.


"You're so desperate," Atwater whispered, his voice a dark, analytical purr against the shell of my ear. He stroked me once, a slow, agonizingly thorough drag from top to bottom that sent a violent shudder through my entire frame. "Your body is flooding with dopamine and oxytocin to combat the cortisol. You are using us as a biological tourniquet."


"I don't care," I gasped, my head falling back against his shoulder, exposing my throat to Blake. "I don't care why. Just do it."


Blake’s mouth immediately descended on the exposed column of my neck. He didn't kiss the skin; he bit it. His teeth scraped against my pulse point, a sharp, borderline painful nip that sent a fresh spike of adrenaline straight to my core, completely devoid of fear. He sucked hard on the sensitive flesh, marking me, branding me with the undeniable proof of his claim.


"We're going to burn her out of your head," Blake promised against my skin, his hands moving to grip my hips, holding me perfectly still for Atwater's incredibly focused assault. "By the time the sun comes up, you aren't going to remember a single name but ours."


Atwater found the sensitive bundle of nerves at my center. He didn't rush. He began a slow, rhythmic pressure, his thumb circling with a terrifyingly precise cadence that seemed engineered specifically to dismantle my cognitive functions.


My hands dropped from Blake's hair, my fingers digging desperately into the sheets. My hips began to move involuntarily, rocking backward into Atwater's hand, chasing the friction, chasing the blinding white heat that was rapidly building at the base of my spine.


"Slow down," Atwater commanded gently, his grip on my waist tightening. "You do not dictate the pace, Callie. You surrender the control. We hold the anchor."


I whimpered, a pathetic, needy sound that I didn't recognize as my own. The denial of momentum was agonizing. I was suspended on a wire, hovering above an abyss of pure sensation, entirely at the mercy of the men holding the line.


Blake pulled back from my neck, his eyes blazing. He reached down between our bodies, his large hand brushing Atwater’s away.


"My turn," Blake growled.


He gripped the thin cotton of my underwear and tore it. The fabric snapped with a loud rip, the sound incredibly violent in the quiet room. He tossed the ruined garment onto the floor.


He didn't bother with his own flannel pants. He shifted his hips, freeing the thick, heavy length of his arousal.


Atwater’s hands returned instantly, his broad palms gripping my thighs, spreading my legs wider across Blake’s lap, opening me completely. Atwater leaned forward, his chest flush against my back, his mouth pressing open-mouthed kisses along the line of my spine.


"Look at me," Blake demanded, his hands gripping my hips tight enough to leave bruises.


I forced my eyes open. My vision was swimming, the edges blurring with the sheer intensity of the impending climax.


"You're ours," Blake stated, a brutal, possessive vow that resonated in the dark.


He lifted my hips a fraction of an inch and pulled me down, burying himself inside me in one smooth, unrelenting upward thrust.


I screamed. The sound tore from my throat, a feral, uninhibited cry that bounced off the thick oak door. The sheer size of him, the absolute fullness stretching me to my absolute physical limit, was a shockwave that obliterated every coherent thought in my brain.


Atwater’s hand instantly clamped over my mouth, stifling the scream against his calloused palm. He wasn't hurting me; he was catching the sound, holding the violence of my release within the confines of the bed.


"Take it," Atwater whispered harshly against my ear, his other hand wrapping tightly around my throat, the pressure firm but entirely safe, a psychological tether keeping me grounded as my body threatened to splinter into a million pieces. "Take all of it."


Blake began to move.


He drove upward, his hips snapping off the mattress with devastating, relentless power. Every thrust was a physical manifestation of his chaotic energy, driving deeper, hitting the exact center of my ache over and over again. The friction was a wildfire.


I couldn't breathe. I couldn't think. I was entirely consumed by the physical reality of the moment. The smell of bourbon. The sweat slicking Blake's chest against mine. The crushing, possessive grip of Atwater's hand on my throat and his palm over my mouth.


I was not a victim. I was not a captive. I was the epicenter of their world.


The tension coiled tighter and tighter, a spring winding down to its absolute snapping point. My nails dug bloody crescents into Blake's shoulders. My eyes rolled back, staring blindly at the dark ceiling.


"Let it go, wildcat," Blake snarled, his pace accelerating, the slap of our bodies echoing wetly in the room. "Give it to me!"


The climax hit me with the force of a high-speed collision.


It started low in my pelvis, a blinding, white-hot detonation of pure pleasure that rippled violently outward, consuming my entire nervous system. I shattered. My body arched rigidly against Atwater, my internal muscles clamping down around Blake in a series of harsh, uncontrollable spasms.


Atwater released my mouth, letting my ragged, sobbing gasp fill the air. He dragged his hand down my throat to cup my breast, his thumb rolling over the tight peak as the aftershocks continued to roll through me.


Blake let out a harsh, guttural roar, his body stiffening. He drove up one final, impossibly deep time, burying himself to the hilt, and held me there as his own climax tore through him. His hot release flooded my core, a heavy, undeniable physical branding that locked me completely to him.


He slumped forward, his heavy chest resting entirely on mine, his breathing coming in ragged, tearing gasps that mirrored my own. His face was buried in the curve of my neck, his lips pressing a final, exhausted kiss against the fading pulse point.


Atwater didn't let go. He kept his arms wrapped securely around us both, his head resting against the back of my shoulder, the slow, steady rhythm of his heartbeat transferring through the skin of my back, acting as a metronome to slow my frantic pulse.


For a long time, the only sound in the room was the harsh, synchronized breathing of three exhausted people, and the relentless, driving patter of the Appalachian rain against the glass.


The panic was gone. The terror of the cartel, the paralyzing memory of Miriam's white office, the fear of the impending war—it had all been burned to ash in the crucible of the bed. My mind was a blank, quiet slate, floating in a heavy, liquid haze of dopamine and exhaustion.


Slowly, Blake shifted his weight. He pulled out of me with a soft, wet sound, easing me off his lap until I slumped sideways onto the tangled charcoal sheets.


I curled onto my side, pulling my knees up slightly, entirely drained of energy.


Atwater moved off the bed. He walked to the small table, picking up the bottle of bourbon. He didn't bother with a glass. He took a long, steady pull directly from the neck, his throat working in the dim light. He set the bottle down, walked back to the bed, and pulled the heavy woolen blanket up, draping it over my bare, cooling skin.


He didn't return to the armchair. He climbed onto the mattress behind me, lying down on his side, fitting his long body perfectly against the curve of my back. He pulled me flush against his chest, sliding one heavy arm around my waist, locking me in place.


Blake lay down on my other side. He reached out, pulling my head onto his chest, his large hand resting protectively over my hip.


I was cocooned in their heat, an impenetrable fortress of muscle and muscle.


Atwater shifted his left hand. His cool, precise fingers moved up my chest, pushing the woolen blanket aside just enough to expose my left collarbone.


I didn't flinch.


He found the jagged edges of the burn scar. He traced it. It wasn't the heavy, commanding claim Darell had staked in the basement. It was a clinical, reverent exploration. He mapped the damaged tissue, committing the geography of my trauma to his memory.


"She used a high-resistance heating element," Atwater murmured in the dark, his voice low, a cold, analytical statement of fact. "Likely an industrial soldering iron or a customized brand. The thermal damage penetrated to the dermal layer."


"Yeah," I whispered, the word heavy and thick with sleep.


"The tactical layout is established," Atwater continued, his fingers still resting lightly over the scar. "Marty has mined the southern access road with C4. Blake has the heavy ordnance staged at the chokepoints. Bruno is tracking their exact vector. When they enter the kill box, we will detonate the perimeter."


He paused, his breath warm against the back of my neck.


"They are not going to reach the house, Callie," Atwater stated, the absolute certainty in his voice a structural beam holding up the ceiling. "They are going to die in the mud. And if Miriam Daniel ever sets foot in this state to find out why her hit squad vanished, Darell will put a bullet in her brain, and I will erase every digital trace of her existence from the servers."


Blake’s hand tightened on my hip, a physical punctuation to the vow.


"We keep what's ours," Blake mumbled sleepily into my hair.


I closed my eyes. The rain drummed relentlessly outside, washing away the tracks in the woods, turning the mountain into an isolated, deadly island.


I had run blindly into the dark, expecting to freeze, expecting to die. Instead, I had fallen into the center of a pack of wolves who had looked at my broken, hunted pieces and decided I was exactly what they wanted to protect.


I drifted into the first deep, dreamless sleep I had experienced in years, anchored entirely by the heavy, breathing weight of the men who had promised me the world, wrapped in copper and skin.
